_comment: RESEARCH-REVIEW backlog — the research/evidence pipeline, NOT trading performance. Split from performance-review-backlog.json 2026-08-30 on the same reasoning as the 2026-05-26 three-way review split: a different RUBRIC wants a different backlog. 'this sweep needs re-running at higher n' and 'this strategy's win rate slipped' are graded against different bars and would bury each other in one file. WHAT BELONGS HERE: a sweep that landed and nobody read; a queue job blocked or underpowered; a harness that produced a number nobody can reproduce; a corpus whose provenance is unclear; an analysis that must be re-run at higher n before it decides anything. WHAT DOES NOT: a strategy tweak (performance), a wiring bug (health), a model promotion (ml). FILE THROUGH scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row, NEVER by hand — it round-trips the exact serialisation and refuses a row restating one already filed.

items.title: 78 landed research units were never read, and the m20 half is largely below its own power floor
items.detail: First run of scripts/research/research_disposition.py --report (2026-08-30) over the two committed corpora: 92 unread / 196 superseded_unread / 0 dispositioned. This session dispositioned the 14 e35 units from RQ-20260830-002, leaving 78 unread, essentially all m20. POPULATION for the power claim: over the newest run per leg, 318 m20 rows carry base_trades_OOS on 317 of them, and 247 sit BELOW the 49.06 floor implied by the queue's own declared power block (n >= (z_a/2 + z_b)^2 / d^2 at alpha=0.05, power=0.80, d=0.4). Observed values run 30-36 with one leg at 4. NOT A BUG IN THE CORPUS - the rows are honest measurements; the finding is that nobody has read them and that most of them cannot answer their own question at the n they hold.
items.why_it_matters: R1-R6 of the research architecture stop at 'landed'; no stage covered 'read', and no review skill referenced the corpora at all (grep returned 0 across all five). So compute was spent, rows were committed, and no decision was ever derived from them. An underpowered unit is worse than an unread one if it is read carelessly: R4's whole point is that an underpowered run manufactures a false finding, and 329 historical honest_negative verdicts already sit at a median OOS base of 33 trades.
items.next_action: In the next /performance-review, work stage 3 of the research-pipeline section: run --unread-only, grade each unit's n_oos against its declared floor FIRST, and disposition it as 'underpowered' (converting to a data-acquisition task) rather than reading a verdict off it. Do not batch-disposition to clear the count - append() refuses a vacuous reason.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when every unit reported 'unread' by research_disposition.py carries a ledger entry with a non-vacuous reason, AND the units graded 'underpowered' have either an enqueued data-acquisition job or a stated reason why more n is unobtainable. Re-running the report and seeing a lower number is NOT sufficient - a superseding run also lowers it.
items.source: first run of the research-disposition ledger
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-02. Every m20 leg carries a real ledger entry, and the supersession that lowered the count was MEASURED benign rather than assumed -- which is the specific evasion this row's criterion forbade. POPULATION: all 218 m20 units over 51 distinct legs in docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl at 943a7192, graded by research_disposition.py. MEASURED: m20 unread = 0 (78 at filing); dispositioned 51; superseded_unread 167. Because 'a superseding run also lowers it', the 167 were PARTITIONED: all 167 have a DISPOSITIONED successor -- gap 0/167 -- so no m20 leg was superseded into silence. Ledger coverage: 51 of 51 distinct m20 legs carry an entry; legs with none: zero. Verdicts 41 underpowered / 10 no_action_warranted, each non-vacuous by construction since append() refuses a non-reason. SECOND HALF of the criterion: 40 of the 41 underpowered entries name a data-acquisition action; the one that does not (ict_scalp_mgc_15m) takes the criterion's other branch and states why more n is unobtainable -- the unit holds a single leg_status=skipped row (data_missing:MGC), and the entry records that the prerequisite is a 15m MGC candle source, so a bare re-dispatch reproduces the skip. INFERRED, NOT MEASURED: that the 78 units named at filing are the same population as the 51 legs now read. I graded the corpus as it stands at 943a7192 and did not reconstruct the 2026-08-30 tree.

items.title: The e35 bracket corpus records no OOS sample size, so its rows cannot be power-graded at all
items.area: research pipeline / M40 R1 results contract
items.detail: R1 of docs/research/RESEARCH-WORKFLOW-ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-27.md makes a row inadmissible unless it carries 'its power: n, and the minimum detectable effect'. MEASURED over the whole e35 corpus (n=8,321 rows, 42 distinct keys): the ONLY key resembling a sample size is `split_target_oos`, present on 377 rows (4.5%) and carrying the value 50 - which is the sweep's TARGET, not the achieved out-of-sample trade count. There is no e35 equivalent of m20's `base_trades_OOS`. CONSEQUENCE, observed not predicted: the disposition ledger graded 78 unread units on 2026-08-30 and could power-grade every m20 unit (10 clearing the 49.06 floor, 40 below it) while 27 e35 units were left UNREAD because there is nothing in the row to grade them against. NOT a defect in the measurements themselves - the R-deltas and gate verdicts are honest; the gap is that the row cannot state the denominator its own verdict rests on.
items.why_it_matters: R4 makes the power gate BLOCKING precisely because an underpowered run costs compute AND manufactures a false finding. A corpus that cannot report n cannot be put through that gate, so every e35 verdict is consumed on trust. This is the same shape as the repo's own 'ALWAYS STATE THE POPULATION' rule: a number whose denominator is unavailable is not quotable, and 8,321 such rows are currently the largest research artifact the fleet holds.
items.next_action: Add the achieved OOS trade count to the e35 extractor (scripts/research/e35_corpus_extract.py) so new rows carry it, and decide explicitly whether historical rows are backfillable from the sweep reports or must stay ungradeable. Do NOT back-fill a zero or the target value - that would assert an observation nobody made, which is the fabrication class provenance.py exists to stop.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when a NEW e35 sweep lands rows carrying an achieved OOS sample size AND research_disposition.py can power-grade them (N_FIELD['e35'] stops being None). Historical rows staying ungradeable is an acceptable outcome IF that is recorded as a deliberate decision rather than left implicit.
items.source: first power-grading pass of the disposition ledger
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-02, both halves verified by measurement rather than by citation. POPULATION: docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl at 943a7192 -- 8,520 rows over 93 sweep stamps and 41 legs. MEASURED: research_disposition.N_FIELD['e35'] == 'base_oos_trades' (no longer None), and 287 rows across 41 sweep stamps carry it. Those 41 stamps all fall on 2026-08-31 (05:50 to 16:26) against a corpus reaching back to 2026-08-23, so the count arrived with a NEW SWEEP rather than the back-fill the row explicitly forbade. research_disposition.py --report now power-grades all 41 e35 units that carry it (observed n_oos 4 to 62). SECOND HALF -- the explicit decision on historical rows -- is recorded at N_FIELD: rows extracted before 2026-08-31 carry no achieved count, cannot be back-filled from a session (the source report.json files are workflow artifacts, not committed), and therefore stay n_oos: null. That is a deliberate recorded decision, which is what the criterion asked for. NEWLY GUARDED: the field choice is now pinned by tests/test_e35_achieved_oos_count.py::test_split_target_oos_still_diverges_from_the_achieved_count, proven to fire -- see BL-20260831-N-FIELDS-DECIDING-MEASUREMENT-IS-RECORDED-BUT-NOT-PINNED.

items.summary: research_queue.observed_n_by_leg keeps the BEST achieved n per leg with no notion of the run configuration that produced it, so a corpus-grounded feasibility check counts observations from a DIFFERENT config as evidence about the one about to run — and on a raise it deadlocks the unit that would produce the new evidence.
items.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-31 while raising e35's `split_target_oos` 50 -> 60 for RQ-20260830-002.

`observed_n_by_leg(corpus)` reduces the corpus to {leg: best n_oos} and `grade_power`'s corpus-grounded branch compares that against the power floor. Nothing in either function knows what run SETTINGS produced an observation, although the corpus rows carry them (`split_target_oos` is a column on every e35 row).

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the dangerous one:
(1) STALE-CONFIG EVIDENCE. After a raise, pre-raise rows remain the best observation for every leg, so a `source: corpus` check grades the NEW config against the OLD config's achieved n.
(2) DEADLOCK. Measured on the 9 capable legs: pre-raise min_per_leg is 46 against a floor of 49.06, so grounding RQ-20260830-002 on the corpus today returns INFEASIBLE and BLOCKS the dispatch — the only thing that would produce post-raise evidence. Scoping observations by config does not fix it either: with zero matching rows the grade flips INFEASIBLE -> UNVERIFIABLE, which also blocks.

⚠️ THE DEADLOCK HALF IS RESOLVED, THE BLINDNESS IS NOT — corrected the same day. This row was filed while `infeasible` was a REFUSAL. Hours later the operator directed leniency ("I'd rather err on the lenient side here and not exclude tests that may [give] some insights"), making `underpowered` and `infeasible` RUNNABLE. There is no deadlock any more: RQ-20260830-002 is now corpus-grounded, grades `infeasible` honestly, RUNS, and will flip to `cleared` on its own once a target-60 run lands ~56 per leg. The earlier workaround (declare `source: none` and have a human come back to switch it) is gone, and with it the 'carried forward in prose' hazard.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is the original finding: observations are still blind to run configuration, so for exactly one cycle after any config change the gate grades the NEW config against OLD rows. Under leniency that is survivable rather than blocking — the unit runs and its verdict is stamped on its rows — but the grade is still wrong for that cycle, and a reader who does not know the raise happened will read the interim `infeasible` as evidence the raise failed. Under a future policy that blocks again, the deadlock returns exactly as described above.
items.resolution_criteria: `observed_n_by_leg` accepts a config scope (e.g. feasibility.observed_where: {split_target_oos: 60}) and counts only rows matching it, verified by a test that a pre-raise row does not satisfy a post-raise scope. ⚠️ The 'must not deadlock' half of the original criterion is NO LONGER the test — leniency removed it — but a scoped check with no matching rows must still resolve to a RUNNABLE state, or re-introducing config-scoping would re-introduce the block by the back door.

updates.note: EXAMINED and NOT ATTEMPTED by the 2026-09-02 drain -- status unchanged, and this is the most tractable row left in this file. It is genuinely closable from a session: the change is a config scope on research_queue.observed_n_by_leg (e.g. feasibility.observed_where: {split_target_oos: 60}) plus a test that a pre-raise row does not satisfy a post-raise scope, and the corpus carries what such a test needs -- MEASURED at 943a7192, split_target_oos is non-null on 566 of 8,520 e35 rows and takes {50: 377, 60: 189}, so a pre-raise (50) and a post-raise (60) population both exist in real data. I left it because it edits the R4 ADMISSION GATE that decides what runs, its runnable-on-no-matching-rows clause needs care (the criterion's own warning about re-introducing the block by the back door), and folding it into a PR built around a different structural class would have made both harder to review. Not blocked -- deferred, with the population above already established for whoever takes it.

items.area: research queue / R5 dispatch + corpus identity
items.summary: Across ALL THREE registered corpora — 9,744 rows — not one carries research_unit or research_power_state. That includes the 44 gld_compat rows written by the queue's ONE confirmed successful dispatch, and there they are unstampable BY CONSTRUCTION: gld-compat-matrix.yml declares no research_unit input at all.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-31 by reading every row of the three corpora that scripts/research/research_disposition.py::CORPORA declares — e35 8,321 rows, m20 1,379, gld_compat 44. `research_unit` is None on 9,744 of 9,744 and `research_power_state` is None on 9,744 of 9,744. STATE THE POPULATION: this is the registered corpora only; a store not in CORPORA was not examined.

THE TWO CAUSES ARE DIFFERENT AND ONLY ONE IS A DEFECT.

(a) e35 (8,321 rows) — NOT a defect. `e35-bracket-sweep.yml` DOES declare `research_unit` and `power_state` inputs and threads them as RESEARCH_UNIT / RESEARCH_POWER_STATE into the extractor step (lines 51, 367-368). Its rows are unstamped simply because no e35 run has ever been dispatched THROUGH the queue — every one was run by hand. The route works and has not been exercised.

(b) gld_compat (44 rows) — THE DEFECT. `gld-compat-matrix.yml` contains no occurrence of `research_unit` anywhere, so it cannot accept the input. `dispatch_queue.py` injects the stamp only when the unit declares `research_unit` (line 183), and RQ-20260827-001 declares none — which is the ONLY reason that dispatch succeeded, since `gh workflow run -f` on an undeclared input is rejected outright. So the conditional injection is load-bearing and correct, AND it means this route's rows can never carry the identity.

WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY. Run 33340458710 (event=schedule, 2026-08-30T22:56:22Z) dispatched RQ-20260827-001 and 11 rows landed in gld-compat-matrix-verdicts.jsonl 28s later — that evidence was used on 2026-08-31 to CLEAR OI-20260827-RESEARCH-QUEUE-DISPATCHER-NEVER-FIRED. The clearance stands: the dispatcher did fire and rows did land. But the rows are UNATTRIBUTABLE to the unit that produced them, so the queue's one proven route delivers exactly the thing the identity exists to prevent — a row from a graded job being byte-indistinguishable from an ungraded one. The extractor's own comment states the contract: 'Empty is NOT-QUEUE-DISPATCHED, never was a test.' Every gld row reads as not-queue-dispatched.

NOT A TEST GAP IN THE OBVIOUS PLACE. tests/test_research_chain_end_to_end.py covers the dispatcher argv, the workflow env and the extractor across their seams, and it passes — because it exercises the e35-shaped path. Nothing asserts that a REGISTERED CORPUS's owning workflow can accept the stamp at all. That is the seam one level out.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (1) gld-compat-matrix.yml gains `research_unit` + `power_state` inputs and its writer stamps them onto every row it emits, verified by a queue-dispatched run whose landed rows carry the unit id — read from the corpus, not from the diff; OR (2) a guard asserts that every workflow named by a `run.workflow` in research/queue/*.yaml whose store is in research_disposition.CORPORA declares the stamp inputs, so the gap announces itself on the commit that creates it rather than in an audit. (2) is the durable half and (1) alone leaves the next route free to repeat it. NOT resolved by a passing unit test: the criterion is a stamped row in a committed corpus.

updates.note: REFUSED by the 2026-09-02 drain -- premise CONFIRMED by measurement, remedy not reachable from this session. MEASURED at 943a7192: research/queue/*.yaml names two workflows whose store is in research_disposition.CORPORA -- e35-bracket-sweep.yml (4 queue units) and gld-compat-matrix.yml (RQ-20260827-001). e35-bracket-sweep.yml declares research_unit and threads it through to RESEARCH_UNIT; gld-compat-matrix.yml declares NEITHER research_unit NOR research_power_state -- its workflow_dispatch inputs are 'strategy' and 'symbol' only. Corpus side, rows carrying both stamps: e35 995 of 8,520; m20 0 of 1,379; gld_compat 0 of 55. The row is right and the gap is live. WHY I DID NOT BUILD CRITERION (2): the guard itself is straightforward, but it FAILS TODAY on gld-compat-matrix.yml -- correctly. Landing it green would need either (a) also editing gld-compat-matrix.yml to declare and stamp the inputs, which is half of criterion (1) WITHOUT the verification (1) explicitly demands ('a queue-dispatched run whose landed rows carry the unit id -- read from the corpus, not from the diff'), and I have no way to dispatch a run; or (b) allowlisting gld-compat-matrix.yml, which ships a green guard over a live defect. (a) is the worse of the two because the guard would then certify a stamp path nobody has observed working. Both are this repo's own filed bug class, so I built neither. FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the guard, the workflow edit and a dispatched gld-compat run read back OUT OF THE CORPUS should land as one change.

items.summary: e35_corpus_extract.measurement_key has NO time component, so a re-sweep SUPERSEDES the prior measurement of the same cell. RQ-20260831-002 is a MONTHLY job whose question is explicitly longitudinal — 'are the shipped cells still behaving as they did when they shipped?' — so running it destroys the baseline it compares against. The job cannot answer its own question from the store it writes to.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-31 on a real queue-dispatched run (research-queue-dispatch 33388490432 -> e35-bracket-sweep 33388518030, landed as #10577), by diffing the corpus at 62641dfb against the post-landing commit.

Population: rows whose `leg` is one of the five the run swept (iwm/mgc/qqq/scha/spy _1d).
  before: 1,035 rows / 995 distinct (leg,cell) / max 2 rows per cell
  after : 1,035 rows / 995 distinct (leg,cell) / max 2 rows per cell
  cells touched by the run: 995, and ALL 995 already had a prior row
  pre-probe rows surviving on a re-swept cell: 40
So ~955 prior measurements are no longer in the corpus. The total is unchanged because each incoming row replaced one.

MECHANISM READ, NOT INFERRED — my first reading of the arithmetic was wrong and I checked. `merge()` builds `by_key = {r['measurement_key']: r for r in existing}` and lets incoming overwrite; its self-test asserts 're-extract supersedes' with superseded=2, added=0. `measurement_key` is `leg|cell|tp_cap_pct|split_mode|split_target_oos` and its own docstring says 'Re-running the same cell supersedes it'. THIS IS DELIBERATE AND DOCUMENTED. The defect is not in the extractor — it is that nobody joined that retention rule to what the monthly job asks. The 40 survivors differ on a key component (35 gated rows carry split_target_oos 50 while the rest carry None), which is the key behaving exactly as documented, NOT evidence that history is kept.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS JOB. `sweep_generated_at` is on every row, so a run is dated — but only the newest row per key survives, so a cell yields ONE timestamp, never a series. Any question of the form 'has this changed since it shipped?' is unanswerable from this corpus by construction, and RQ-20260831-002 is that question, on a monthly cadence, with a power.feasibility block that already concedes it cannot be powered. It would accumulate nothing: each month's run erases the prior month's row for the same cell.

NOT CLAIMED: that the m20 corpus shares this. Its N_FIELD and key were not examined.
items.resolution_criteria: A DECISION recorded, then implemented — this is a design call, not a one-line fix. The options are (a) add a time component to measurement_key so re-sweeps accumulate, which grows the store without bound and needs a retention policy of its own; (b) keep superseding but write the superseded row to a history sidecar; (c) accept it and REWRITE RQ-20260831-002's question so it no longer claims to be longitudinal, since an accrual job that erases its own accrual is worse than no job. Resolved when the choice is written down with its reason AND a re-sweep is observed to leave the prior measurement readable (a) or (b), or the job's question no longer asks for it (c). A passing extractor test is not the criterion: the criterion is two dated measurements of one cell readable at the same time, or a question that does not need them.

updates.note: REFUSED by the 2026-09-02 drain -- out of reach, not unexamined. The criterion needs a recorded DESIGN DECISION plus an observed re-sweep leaving the prior measurement readable ('two dated measurements of one cell readable at the same time, or a question that does not need them'). I cannot dispatch a sweep, and the choice between (a) a time component in measurement_key, (b) the history sidecar and (c) rewriting RQ-20260831-002's question is a design call above a drain's remit. WHAT I DID MEASURE, because it bears directly on the choice: route (b) is already partly built and is currently UNSOUND. docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus-history.jsonl holds 10,547 rows (15.3 MB against the live corpus's 11.4 MB), but 5,373 of them (50.9%) are the archiving run's OWN rows -- 100.0% of those 5,373 are simultaneously live at the same sweep stamp, against 0.0% of the genuinely-displaced half. So the sidecar does not yet give a reader two dated measurements of one cell; it gives them one measurement written twice. Anyone choosing (b) must fix BL-20260831-CORPUS-JOB-SCANS-EVERY-LEG-REPORT-TWICE-SO-THE-HISTORY-SIDECAR-ARCHIVES-THE-RUNS-OWN-ROWS first, or they will be reasoning about a store that half-duplicates itself.

items.summary: 28 of the 42 unread e35 units carry NO achieved OOS count at all (`base_oos_trades` null on every row), so the R4 power gate cannot grade them -- and they cannot be back-filled: the source report.json files are workflow artifacts, never committed, and a PM-side session has no artifact download. They are therefore stuck in `unread` indefinitely. The verdict vocabulary (actioned / no_action_warranted / underpowered / superseded) has no member for NEVER MEASURED. Recording them `underpowered` would assert a measurement nobody made -- it means 'measured, and too small' -- so the honest options today are to leave them unread (which reads as nobody looked) or to re-sweep, a multi-hour run the corpus exists to avoid. That is a collapsed state in the vocabulary itself: 'we measured n and it was short' and 'n was never recorded' are different facts with different remedies (acquire more data vs re-run the extractor).
items.evidence: Measured 2026-08-31 over docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl via research_disposition.survey(). 42 unread units: 14 gradeable (n_oos 4..50), 28 with n_oos null. Of the 14, ALL were dispositioned this session -- 1 no_action_warranted (trend_donchian_sol_4h, n=50) and 13 underpowered -- leaving exactly the 28 ungradeable ones. The CORPORA docstring in research_disposition.py already records why the back-fill is impossible ('rows extracted before 2026-08-31 carry no achieved count and CANNOT be back-filled from a session'); what it does not say is that this leaves those units with no legal disposition.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER a fifth verdict (e.g. `ungradeable`) exists and is refused as a terminal close, so a reader can record 'this unit predates the achieved-n stamp' without asserting a measurement -- with a test pinning it distinct from `underpowered` -- OR the 28 legs are re-swept and become gradeable, with the count of still-ungradeable units measured and stated afterwards. Closing this by recording the 28 as `underpowered` is NOT acceptable and is the specific outcome this row exists to prevent.

updates.note: REFUSED by the 2026-09-02 drain -- status deliberately UNCHANGED, and THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. POPULATION: all 97 e35 units over 41 distinct legs in docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl at 943a7192. (1) THE COUNT HAS MOVED: units carrying no achieved OOS count are 56, not 28. I did not reconstruct the 2026-08-31 tree, so I cannot say whether 28 was wrong then or the corpus has since grown; 56 is what is true now. (2) THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: all 56 ungradeable units are in state superseded_unread -- 56/56 -- and all 41 gradeable units are dispositioned. Every one of the 41 e35 legs has a LATEST stamp carrying the count; e35 legs never carrying it on any stamp: ZERO. (3) WHAT THAT REFUTES: the row's first branch asks for a fifth verdict 'ungradeable' so a reader can record 'this unit predates the achieved-n stamp' without asserting a measurement. But a reader dispositions the NEWEST run per leg -- that is what superseded_unread means, reading an older one is moot by the mechanism's own design. The ungradeable set and the moot set are currently THE SAME 56 UNITS, so the new verdict would have no unit a reader could legitimately apply it to. Building it ships vocabulary with no reachable use: the mirror image of a permanently-green guard, and the same waste. (4) The row's second branch -- re-sweep the legs -- is already satisfied for every leg a reader will actually meet: 41 of 41 latest stamps are gradeable. (5) WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS ROW LIVE AGAIN, and why it stays OPEN rather than being closed: a leg swept ONLY before 2026-08-31 would have an ungradeable LATEST stamp and would land unread AND ungradeable -- precisely the state the vocabulary cannot express. There are zero such legs today. Re-grade this row when that count is next non-zero. NOT MEASURED: I cannot dispatch a sweep, so I could not create that state to observe the mechanism's behaviour in it.

items.summary: `load_units` aggregates a unit's rows with OPPOSITE discipline on two fields that both feed the same power judgement. `power_state` is worst-state-wins, with a comment explaining that one clean row must not launder an accrual-tainted unit. `n_oos` two lines later is `max(u['n_oos'] or 0, int(v))` -- the most generous aggregator -- with no comment at all. If a unit's rows ever carried differing achieved-n values, the single largest would decide whether the unit clears the 49.06 floor, which is the same laundering the field above forbids.
items.evidence: Measured 2026-08-31: harmless TODAY and only by luck. Across all 14 gradeable unread e35 units, exactly 7 of 199 rows (3.5%) carry `base_oos_trades`, and each unit has exactly ONE distinct value -- those 7 rows are precisely the GATED rows (verified: the cell set carrying an achieved-n is identical to the cell set carrying a gate_verdict), because only a gated cell has an OOS split. So max() currently picks from a one-element set. The reading trap is separate and real: n_oos describes the GATED SUBSET, not the unit -- a reader who takes `n_oos=50` as the unit's evidence base is reading a number off 3.5% of the rows. This session nearly dispositioned trend_donchian_sol_4h on that misreading and caught it only by checking the denominator.
items.resolution_criteria: `n_oos` either documents why max() is correct for a leg-level constant, or becomes min()/worst-state-wins to match its neighbour; AND the reported field states its own denominator (e.g. rows_with_n beside n_oos) so a consumer cannot read a gated-subset statistic as the unit's. A test pins whichever discipline is chosen.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-02 -- and the FIRST HALF OF THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. POPULATION: all 315 units of the two power-graded corpora at 943a7192 (e35 97, m20 218). MEASURED: 258 units carry at least one achieved OOS count (41 e35, 217 m20); on every one of those 258 the values across the unit's rows are IDENTICAL -- units where n_oos varies: ZERO. So max(), min() and worst-state-wins return the same number on 258/258, and changing max() to min() 'to match its neighbour' would have altered no output anywhere on the live corpus. n_oos is a leg-level constant; max() is RETAINED and its justification is now measured rather than assumed. THE DENOMINATOR HALF WAS THE LIVE DEFECT AND IS FIXED: on e35 the count is carried by 7 of a unit's 199 rows -- 3.52%, on 41 of 41 graded units -- while --report printed 'rows=199 n_oos=49' on one line, handing a reader a statistic and a denominator 28x too large. survey() now emits rows_with_n per unit and --report renders 'n_oos=49/7r'. PINNED AND PROVEN TO FAIL, not assumed: tests/test_research_disposition_denominator.py. Dropping rows_with_n from survey() fails 2 tests; hard-zeroing it fails 1; planting ONE varying base_trades_OOS row into the live m20 corpus fails the constancy assertion. Baseline green after each restore.

items.not_a_duplicate_of: BL-20260831-E35-CORPUS-SUPERSEDES-THE-BASELINE-ITS-MONTHLY-JOB-ASKS-ABOUT (lexical overlap 0.67, read before filing). That row is a WRITE/RETENTION defect -- measurement_key has no time component, so a re-sweep destroys the prior measurement -- and its remedy shipped as the history sidecar. This row is a READ/POWER defect: nothing is being destroyed, the rows are all present, and they cannot be GRADED because the batch holding them predates the achieved-n stamp. Same subsystem and near-identical vocabulary; different mechanism, different remedy, and the sidecar does not touch it.
items.summary: The e35 corpus's positive results and its readable results are DISJOINT SETS, and the disposition mechanism can currently only read the empty one. items.summary: The e35 sweep's `corpus` job scans every leg's report.json TWICE, so the history sidecar shipped by #10583 archives 51% same-run duplicates instead of superseded measurements. Measured on run 33411906178, the sidecar's FIRST live exercise: 10,547 archived rows, of which 5,174 are genuine supersedes (per-leg source path, keys still live in the corpus carrying the new measurement) and 5,373 are copies of THAT RUN'S OWN rows (source path under `collected/e35-bracket-ALL/`). 5,373 is exactly 27 legs x ~199 cells -- every row the run produced, written twice and archived once.
items.evidence: Mechanism, confirmed by the `source` field rather than inferred: the `aggregate` job uploads artifact `e35-bracket-ALL` with `path: collected`, which CONTAINS a copy of every per-leg artifact directory. The `corpus` job then downloads with `pattern: e35-bracket-*` (line 356), which matches the 27 per-leg artifacts AND `e35-bracket-ALL`, so `rglob('report.json')` finds each leg's report at two paths. Two rows, identical `measurement_key`, so `merge()` supersedes one and the sidecar archives it. Sample key `gld_pullback_1d|tp2.5_to400|0.099|None|None`: archived and live rows differ in EXACTLY three fields -- `source` (ALL path vs per-leg path), `superseded_at`, `superseded_by_sweep` -- i.e. the same measurement. Archive source-path census: per-leg 5,174 / ALL 5,373. Corpus source-path census: per-leg 8,520 / ALL 0, so the CORPUS IS CLEAN and the measurement is uncorrupted -- only the archive's meaning is. The `aggregate` job at line 261 is unaffected: it runs BEFORE `e35-bracket-ALL` exists (it uploads it), so its own rollup sees each report once. This has been latent since the corpus job was added 2026-08-23; it was invisible until #10583 gave the displaced rows somewhere to land.
items.why_it_matters: The sidecar exists so a re-sweep cannot destroy the prior measurement. It does that correctly -- the 5,174 genuine supersedes are all present. But a reader asking the question the archive was BUILT to answer, 'what did the previous measurement say?', gets for half the rows the same run's own output, stamped `superseded_by_sweep` with the timestamp of the run that produced it. A self-superseding row is not a prior measurement, and nothing in the file distinguishes the two populations except the `source` path, which no consumer reads.
items.resolution_criteria: The next e35 sweep writes a history sidecar in which every archived row's `superseded_by_sweep` names a DIFFERENT run than its own `sweep_generated_at`, and the archived count equals the number of keys genuinely displaced. Proposed remedy, one line and structural: rename the aggregate artifact so the corpus job's glob cannot match it (`e35-bracket-ALL` -> a name outside `e35-bracket-*`), which stops the duplicate being produced rather than de-duplicating it afterwards. A dedup inside `e35_corpus_extract.py` keyed on `measurement_key` would also work and is more robust to a future artifact name, but it hides the double-download rather than removing it. NOT closed by reasoning about the workflow: it needs an actual sweep whose sidecar is read back.

MECHANISM VERIFIED, NOT INFERRED, with a positive and a negative control: of the 5,373 self-archived rows, 5,373 (100.0%) have a measurement_key that is ALSO live in docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl AT THE SAME SWEEP STAMP -- the run archived rows it simultaneously kept. The self-archived rows all carry 2026-08-31 stamps at 199 rows per stamp. This confirms the row's diagnosis and its proposed one-line remedy (rename the aggregate artifact out of the e35-bracket-* glob) addresses the right mechanism. OI-20260831-42-RESEARCH-UNITS-ARE-UNREAD called that pile 'the same defect in the past tense', and this row exists to record that the claim is NOT established -- and that today produced direct evidence against it being uniformly true.
items.evidence: A unit is `superseded_unread` when a NEWER run stamp exists for the same (corpus, leg) and the older one was never dispositioned. On 2026-08-31 this session created 27 of them itself, and created them by doing exactly the right thing: the 2026-08-29 target-50 measurements of 27 legs were superseded by a target-60 re-sweep that WAS read and dispositioned, with each prior passing cell addressed by name in the successor's reason text. Those 27 are not unread results; they are the expected residue of re-measuring at adequate power. The count moved 229 -> 256 across that work, i.e. every one of the 27 added is accounted for. What is NOT established is the other 229: nobody has checked whether each was superseded by a measurement that was itself read, or whether some were superseded by a run that also went unread -- which would be a genuine gap and is the only part of this pile that is a defect.
items.why_it_matters: The number is large and looks alarming, and a review session reading `superseded_unread: 256` beside `unread: 0` can reasonably conclude the pile was swept under a rug. It was not, at least not for the 27 this session can speak to. But asserting the whole 256 is benign would be exactly the unprovenanced conclusion this repo keeps paying for, so the honest state is that ~11% is demonstrably benign and 89% is UNMEASURED -- not benign, and not a defect either.
items.resolution_criteria: A one-shot pass over the ledger + corpora that partitions the 256 into (a) superseded by a run stamp that IS dispositioned -- benign, the re-measurement residue; and (b) superseded by a run stamp that is ITSELF unread or superseded -- a real gap, since no measurement of that leg was ever read. Only (b) is work. Reporting a bare count again, in either direction, does not resolve this. NOT closed by re-running --report.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-02 -- the partition delivered as a committed tool rather than a one-shot number, so it can be re-run instead of re-derived. POPULATION: all 370 units across the three corpora at 943a7192; superseded_unread = 256, unchanged from filing. MEASURED via 'research_disposition.py --superseded-partition': (a) BENIGN -- the newest run for the leg IS dispositioned -- 223/256 = 87.1%; (b) GAP -- the newest run is itself unread, so no measurement of that leg was ever read -- 33/256 = 12.9%. The gap is entirely gld_compat (e35 0/56, m20 0/167, gld_compat 33/33) and it reduces to ONE action: all 33 sit beneath the 11 gld_compat legs whose newest run (2026-08-31T17:20:54) is the current unread pile, so dispositioning those 11 units clears the whole gap half. AN AMBIGUITY IN THE CRITERION, RESOLVED AND RECORDED: 'superseded by a run stamp that is ITSELF unread or superseded' can mean the leg's LATEST stamp or each unit's IMMEDIATE successor. Both were computed and they differ by ~5x -- latest: 33 gap; immediate-successor: 161 gap. The LATEST reading is the one the criterion's own rationale requires ('since no measurement of that leg was ever read'): a unit three re-sweeps back whose leg was eventually read is benign, and counting each intermediate link of such a chain inflates the answer by 128. The immediate-successor figure is recorded here so a later reader does not rediscover the discrepancy and conclude one of us miscounted. NOT VACUOUS: both halves are non-zero, the controls in tests/test_research_disposition_denominator.py plant a gap and a benign successor separately and assert the partition tells them apart, and blanking superseded_by_state in survey() fails the live test.
